speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The TA provides the Info-communications Media Development Authority (IMDA) with various powers, including those to grant licences, issue directions and codes of practices, and promulgate service standards.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Since the last review in 2012, my Ministry has been keeping a close watch on how the industry has evolved, both locally and internationally, as well as the changing needs and demands of Singapore consumers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: First, the reliance on telecom services by consumers and businesses, especially for mobile telephone services, has increased dramatically over the last few years.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Hence, consumers and businesses have come to expect more reliable and better quality service standards.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: To meet these rising demands, IMDA must have the ability to facilitate the continued deployment of telecoms infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Second, consumer disputes have become more individualised in nature and usually relate to customer-specific contractual and billing issues.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Given the individualised nature of these disputes, IMDA's existing frameworks for consumer protection will not be as effective.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: A dedicated, specialised and independent platform that can resolve these disputes in a fair and even-handed way will be needed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Lastly, my Ministry has noted instances where end users may not have the freedom to access telecoms services from their preferred operator.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It has been 16 years since the telecoms sector was fully liberalised.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: A key consideration for liberalisation was to allow end users more choice.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: To ensure that consumers and businesses can continue to reap the benefits of competition, any obstacles in the way of them exercising choice should be removed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Respondents generally supported our observations and suggested solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In light of this, we intend to amend the TA to effect most of these proposals, save for two.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As we have experienced a recent spike in the number of cable-cut incidents around Singapore, we wanted to send a clear and strong deterrent signal to would-be cable-cut offenders that they must follow the prescribed procedures for isolating telecom cables before commencing earthworks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The other proposal that we will not proceed with is requiring that all appeals to the Minister also be copied to the regulator.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Such a requirement is an operational one and need not feature in primary legislation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Today, IMDA's Code of Practice for Info-communication Facilities in Buildings, also known as the COPIF, requires building developers and owners to provide adequate space and facilities for the deployment of telecoms equipment in their buildings.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: However, IMDA has faced many practical challenges with building managers that have delayed timely deployments in the buildings they manage.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: To ensure COPIF's effectiveness, clause 2 will expressly clarify that parties who have control over the day-to-day management and operations of the building must also comply with COPIF.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In practice, IMDA will continue to enforce COPIF requirements on the legal owner of the building in the first instance, before reaching out to building managers, such as the Management Corporations and Town Councils.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In addition, under current rules, telecom licensees must provide sufficient notice when entering buildings to deploy their infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Clause 8 will provide greater certainty to building owners and occupiers on this notification and objection process.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, before entering a building, licensees must first issue clear and accurate notifications to the building owner stating their intent and nature of the activities to be done, including whether they intend to use the space and facilities to serve any other building.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In our dense urban environment, mobile deployments need to be sited at suitably high locations, such as building rooftops and towers, to optimise coverage of each mobile antenna.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Accordingly, it is usually optimal for mobile operators to deploy their infrastructure on rooftops to serve multiple buildings from one location.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Given the advantages that spring-boarding confers, clauses 9 and 10 will empower IMDA to establish a framework to further regulate and facilitate the use of and access to buildings for spring-boarding.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Following these amendments, IMDA will consult affected stakeholders on amendments to COPIF to allow spring-boarding and other related operational details.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This amendment simply prevents a building owner from denying end users the right to choose their preferred operator.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The amendment is also not intended to apply to data centres, central offices and telecom exchanges, as their customers lease space to locate their equipment and are not considered tenants or residents for the purpose of this provision.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: To ensure that clauses 9, 10 and 11 are effective, IMDA will be able to issue written notices and directions to licensees, developers, owners or occupiers of any land or building to achieve regulatory compliance.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Although no concerns were raised in relation to these powers during the public consultation, I wish to assure the House that IMDA will be reasonable, prudent and Page: 20 circumspect in the application of these powers and that IMDA will take affected parties' concerns into account before making a decision.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA will also only narrowly apply these powers to specific contractual clauses that are inconsistent with the written notice or direction.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In all other cases, these amendments to the TA will not affect the continuance of existing contracts, which should carry on until the expiry or termination.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Given that IMDA's regulatory powers for the telecom and media sectors are contained in the TA and IMDA Act respectively, clauses 17 and 21 will make amendments to both, to give IMDA powers to establish an ADR framework, as well as the rules, procedures and operational mechanics of the ADR scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As I mentioned during the debate on the IMDA Bill in August this year, having telecom and media regulation in separate legislation is an interim measure and my Ministry remains committed to the longer term approach of developing a holistic framework for the infocomm media sector through streamlined rules and regulations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA is considering a suitable and independent operator for the ADR scheme and will consult relevant stakeholders on the details of the scheme after the legislative framework is in place.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Clause 2 will amend the current definition of "telecommunication service" to make explicit that this includes the leasing of telecom cables.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Clauses 3, 4 and 5 will amend sections 5, 5A and 5B respectively to clarify IMDA's existing powers to levy fees and charges for licences, spectrum rights and satellite orbital slots.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These amendments are to clarify IMDA's existing powers and are not intended to grant any new powers or impose any new obligations on regulated persons.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Clauses 3, 5 and 6 will also make it clear that a licensee is not entitled to a refund of licence fees if its licence is suspended, cancelled, terminated or reduced in duration by IMDA or at the request of the licensee.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Similarly, clause 18 will clarify that it is an offence for a telecom licensee whose licence has been suspended to establish, install, maintain or operate a telecoms system or service.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Clause 7 inserts a new section to provide that where a person uses shared radio frequencies, that person must accept that interference may occur and that IMDA is not liable for any interference.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This amendment is no different from the principles governing the sharing of radio frequencies already set out in IMDA's Telecommunications (Radio-communication) Regulations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Nonetheless, before allocating radio frequencies for sharing, IMDA will continue to carefully consider and assess the impact and whether there will be potential for interference to existing users.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This amendment is in line with exceptions already set out in the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) and will be applicable for instances, such as Page: 21 network planning, maintenance, as well as for facilitating interconnection and interoperability between telecoms licensees.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Aside from these purposes, the PDPA will continue to apply.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: My Ministry has also proposed a suite of enhancements to provide greater clarity to the sections of the TA relating to consolidations and corporate governance.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Clause 14 will clarify the specific circumstances in which IMDA's directions with respect to consolidations have overriding effect.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Clause 16 takes into account industry comments from the public consultation and clarifies the specific conditions that IMDA may impose for its approval of CEO or Board of Director appointments in designated telecoms licensees.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Lastly, clause 20 will allow IMDA to issue regulations on the wiring of telecoms cables in access networks deployed by telecoms system licensees.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Such regulations are currently limited to the public switched telephone networks belonging to public telecoms licensees which rely on copper cables.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The amendment ensures that IMDA's regulatory framework for the deployment of telecoms cables stays relevant as copper cables are increasingly being phased out and replaced by optical fibre cables.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA is committed to working closely with the industry and various stakeholders to develop the necessary operational and implementation details relating to these proposed amendments.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: My Ministry will continue to stay abreast of developments, both locally and internationally, to ensure that our legislative and regulatory frameworks continue to facilitate a conducive environment for businesses to grow and thrive and for consumers to benefit from competitive and high quality services.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Further, would the Ministry consider a strategy for all the operators to share base stations, like how operators currently use the NetLink Trust infrastructure for fibre broadband, for example?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, you do not clog up your rooftops with too many base stations or you have too many inline within the building repeater cells, for example.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This may be especially important if they are moving to a new 5G network in the future based on new infrastructure, thus sharing may provide economies of scale for the operators and be more cost-effective for consumers, too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: On this point about access to rooftop space, there are already existing agreements in place to govern this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How will the Ministry protect landlords with these existing agreements in place?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I ask Page: 22 this as I wonder if the new regulations will enable operators to cancel these existing agreements with immediate effect and request to relocate their base stations in the same building under new terms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The other area I would like to raise a point on is the proposal to empower IMDA to establish an Alternative Dispute Resolution scheme.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I applaud this scheme but seek more clarity on how it will be implemented.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will the ADR scheme be administered by the Government?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What sorts of disputes can consumers bring to the ADR operator?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How is the proposed ADR scheme different from some of the existing mediation channels available to consumers today, such as CASE or the Singapore Mediation Centre?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These are important questions to ask and gain clarity on.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: First, with regard to health; second, with regard to access; and third, with regard to safety.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In terms of health, with the growing number of space stations and telecommunications access points in Singapore, there is some concern on the ground on impact on human health.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: According to the American Cancer Society, people exposed to radiofrequency radiation can be affected and there are potential health risks.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Recently, in South Korea, there have also been a series of protests against THAAD system – which the American military would be deploying – which is based on radio signals and telecommunications signals.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Overall, it is supposed to protect South Korea against any hostile North Korean aggression.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Some of those I have spoken to felt that this was quite overarching in terms of the number of Acts that it overrides and grants access to many of these private buildings.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Therefore, could the Minister perhaps explain whether there has been any response during the public feedback with regard to granting of access and whether there are some key areas of hindrance?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In terms of cable-cut incidents that the Minister has mentioned earlier, many of these equipment are based in public buildings, some of which would be HDB blocks.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Access to rooftops of these buildings can sometimes be circumvented.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, on how many occasions over the past three years have the authority authorised the works to be carried out, despite the objections and following the inquiry?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify how long the telecommunications licensee is given to try to resolve the dispute?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And is there a timeframe provided for the Authority to hold an inquiry from the time a written objection is lodged?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I expect that most of the time, there should not be strong reasons for objection, but, in some cases, owners could have legitimate reservations and this should be promptly looked into.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that the installation of mobile equipment is primarily for the economic benefit of mobile operators.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With this in mind, would the Ministry consider ensuring that operators ensure a guaranteed minimum standard of broadband service to all customers?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This would go beyond service levels on coverage, but include a requirement on speed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, all 4G customers within a certain area of an installed mobile broadband equipment should be guaranteed a certain Internet speed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If speeds fall below a certain level, the operator must respond within a certain time to remedy any issues.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Such a regulated guarantee would also provide more comfort to owners that the equipment installed on their roofs will benefit them as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Third, a minor point on an inconvenience faced by consumers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Consumers should have a choice on which networking equipment they can use, now that amendments have been proposed for Internet and mobile operators to have a choice on where best to install their equipment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Page: 24 Currently, Internet Service Providers (ISPs) often require customers to use a default modem and router, which is rented or bought from the ISP.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This means that if the customer has an existing router or modem, they will not be allowed to use it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, unless you are subscribing to the most expensive plan, SingTel currently requires that you use their own modem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I had a personal experience with this inconvenience.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, when my ISP's support came, I was told that I would not be able to use it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I ended up buying a device which I was not allowed to use in my own home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Speaking up on behalf of consumers, would the Ministry consider taking steps to change this?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Given the rapid developments in the telecommunications and media industries, the proposed amendments to the Telecommunications Act (TA) and Media Development Authority of Singapore Act (MDAA) are, indeed, timely.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Allow me to first talk about the proposed amendments to the Additional Dispute Resolution mechanism.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is laudable that IMDA is taking proactive steps to strengthen consumer protection.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have been approached by many residents who have outstanding issues with the telcos.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For various reasons, they did not or could not use the current dispute resolution mechanisms.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Therefore, I think it is useful to create an alternative.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A meaningful dispute resolution mechanism needs to: be affordable for individual complainants; accommodate consumers of all language and educational backgrounds; run efficiently, with conclusions reached in a timely manner; create binding outcomes; and generate more benefits than it costs to run.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The mandated mediation sessions are conducted by Registrars.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Therefore, affordable mediation services conducted by neutral professionals are already available.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A related and pertinent question is the funding of the ADR.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What volume of cases does IMDA expect to refer to the ADR?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And if small, this raises questions about economies of scale.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Who will pay for the overheads, as well as the direct legal costs of engaging mediators?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Will these costs eventually be passed on to the consumer in the form of higher bills?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: ADR must be accessible to members of the public.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many people, especially the elderly, may be intimidated by the legal process.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They might worry about costs or about complex arguments, especially if their primary language is not English.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: ADR must be simple enough such that aunties and uncles from the heartlands can navigate without fear.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: IMDA must create a standardised process for dispute resolution with clear guidelines.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For example, will there be a fixed timeline, to prevent either side playing for time?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Conversely, we need Page: 25 to safeguard against frivolous or vexatious cases.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Consumers who lodge clearly baseless cases could be penalised, but what qualifies as baseless and how will IMDA set the bar?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A second aspect of the proposed amendments to the TA deals with Mobile Deployment Spaces on rooftops.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mobile services are integral to our daily lives.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We now expect to stream high definition video while sitting in an MRT train.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This demand for bandwidth will only continue to grow as services and consumers get more sophisticated.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I, therefore, laud the IMDA for securing rooftop space for deploying national infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As we always do in land-scarce Singapore, we will need to balance competing demands for rooftop space, and rooftop space is already hotly contested.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Essential utilities like water tanks, recreational facilities like rooftop gardens, and clean energy sources like solar panels – these are all potentially valid alternative uses.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: IMDA needs to navigate the balancing act on two levels.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How will the allocation of Mobile Development Space be determined?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How will IMDA work in tandem with the other relevant agencies, such as HDB, EMA, URA and others, to determine the optimal allocation of space?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And how does IMDA intend to "future proof" this?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many rooftop installations are long-term infrastructure assets that cannot easily be removed.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Commercial rooftop solar panels make this more complex.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Space for services means forgone revenues – a quantifiable opportunity cost.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How does IMDA intend to protect the property rights of the building owners?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Second, how will space be allocated amongst various telecommunications providers?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How will we ensure that such arrangements survive future developments, such as new market entry?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have seen infrastructure and network sharing arrangements become standard industry practice in many countries.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Telcos can choose to share only the passive elements, such as towers and masts, or include the network elements in the sharing arrangements.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Would IMDA consider encouraging our telcos in this direction to mitigate the space constraints that we face?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Apart from space allocation, there is also the issue of costs.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Building owners may have improved their rooftops, for example, through waterproofing.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The deployment of mobile assets may affect or damage such arrangements.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How does IMDA intend to establish reasonable cost allocation measures?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I think a clearer set of rules at the outset will help to minimise this problem in the future.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is prudent for IMDA to closely regulate mergers and acquisitions in the telecommunications industry.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As previously noted, telecommunications services are an essential service and national infrastructure must be safeguarded.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: At the same time, we need to maintain the effectiveness of assets to foreign investors.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Winners today are often forgotten tomorrow and cross-border investment is common, which can be beneficial.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our own telcos themselves are Page: 26 significant regional players.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How do we ensure that greater enforcement will lead to greater welfare, broadly defined?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The same considerations apply at the CEO or Board level.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: On what criteria will IMDA decide to not approve a potential CEO or board member?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Will companies have sufficient insight into the process to adequately prepare their positions?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: My response will focus on Members' comments which are directly related to the Bill at hand.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Mr Ong Teng Koon asked about the overall administration and design of the ADR scheme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As this is the first time such a scheme is being rolled out by IMDA, IMDA will learn from other jurisdictions with similar programmes and consult affected stakeholders to ensure that the scheme meets their needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Both Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Mr Ong Teng Koon also asked how the proposed ADR scheme improves upon existing dispute resolution platforms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, Madam, consumers can bring their disputes to general purpose platforms, such as the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE), the Singapore Mediation Centre and the Small Claims Tribunal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our proposed scheme will differ in two ways, Madam.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As such, disputes usually relate to specific billing and contractual issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Having a dedicated scheme that is familiar with the technicalities of service plans and packages will help to ensure a smoother process for all parties involved.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And this is unlike participation in the existing media platform which is voluntary, aside from the Small Claims Tribunal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And the ADR outcomes will also be binding where Page: 27 settlements are reached.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Although only approximately 400 disputes were escalated to IMDA in 2015, the actual number of disputes is likely to be higher, as some subscribers may have given up on pursuing their disputes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, Madam, in order to contain the costs of running the ADR scheme and, of course, to ensure its sustainability, IMDA is exploring the possibility of appointing existing mediation service providers, such as CASE, to help us in rolling out the scheme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will allow us to share overheads and, of course, more importantly, skilled mediators across platforms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These details, Madam, will be further consulted on once the legislative framework is in place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The details of how IMDA will operationalise these powers will still need to be studied in consultation with stakeholders, as the issues on the ground can be complex and addressing them directly in legislation will not be straightforward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, once the Bill is passed, we will commence this consultation exercise through its review of COPIF so that we could get further feedback from the industry and the licensees.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamed also asked how the amendments will affect existing contractual agreements between building owners and mobile operators for mobile deployments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In relation to the Member's example of a mobile operator cancelling his existing contract in order to relocate to the same building so that they get rent-free, I understand that similar cases were raised when COPIF was first introduced in 2013.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But since then, IMDA has not seen such cases being surfaced.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Removing and reinstalling mobile equipment is, indeed, very expensive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mobile operators are also hesitant to accept protracted disruptions to their mobile coverage while a new contract is being negotiated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The bottomline is that it is not in their favour to do the relocation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Mr Ong Teng Koon also asked how the optimal allocation of Mobile Deployment Space (MDS) and associated costs of mobile deployment on rooftops are determined.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To clarify, Madam, the COPIF today already requires that building owners provide a specific amount of rent-free MDS to mobile operators upon request and that mobile operators compensate the building owners for the associated costs of mobile deployments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, Madam, the total amount of MDS aside, the principles of allocating MDS amongst multiple mobile operators and the framework for compensating costs associated with the mobile deployments will remain consistent with existing COPIF practices for a start.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Any unresolved dispute between the building owners and mobile operators over issues, such as competing uses or compensation, can also be escalated to IMDA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will then work with relevant agencies to strike a balance between the property rights of the building owners and the provision of good quality telecoms services to the public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Page: 28 So, whenever there are disputes, we will step in.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will basically bring the parties in and see what is the best solution possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I agree with the Member that we need to provide the best coverage possible for our consumers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, IMDA facilitates the sharing of certain infrastructure amongst licensees where it is technically challenging to replicate or there are physical constraints.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And this includes the sharing of spaces on existing monopoles and cell towers, as well as sharing mobile deployments in places, such as MRT tunnels.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For MDS in buildings, the COPIF currently limits the total amount of mobile deployment space that is set aside.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And where there are multiple operators competing for the same space, this space must be shared amongst them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: If additional space is required, the mobile operators would have to commercially negotiate for more from the building owners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA has been able to resolve most cases through informal mediation, without having to issue any formal directions for the works to be carried out.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As for timelines, the TA does not state a fixed timing for resolving disputes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Each case is unique and IMDA will set a reasonable amount of time for all parties to reach a happy resolution.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we will step in as quickly as possible to make sure we can resolve the dispute.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Lastly, Mr Ong Teng Koon asked how IMDA balances between the benefits of foreign investment and the need to protect national interests when regulating mergers and acquisitions, as well as when approving CEO and Board of Director appointments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, IMDA does maintain oversight over such transactions and appointments to ensure that they do not cause significant harm to market competition, consumers and public interest.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is narrower than the existing section 32(d) as directions could previously take effect despite any written law.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And these amendments were presented during public consultation but we did not receive any comments on this part.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As these issues are not directly related to the Bill at hand, I invite the Members to file separate Parliamentary Questions and I would be happy to discuss these in Parliament.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am confident that this Bill will ensure that the TA continues to remain relevant and effective for regulating the telecommunications industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Page: 29 Moving forward, my Ministry and IMDA are committed to working closely with the industry and various stakeholders to develop and implement these amendments in detail and to creating a conducive regulatory environment for both businesses and consumers.
